experience.title: Software Development Manager
summary: Engineering hire #1. Built the technical side from the ground up.
Took products from early concepts to working business in logistics and software.
Bridged the gap between dev and the rest of the company, making sure what was built matched what the business needed.
Designed logistics platforms that held up under real pressure, led UI/UX for web and early mobile, and helped junior devs find their feet as the team grew.

careerNotes: ParcelVision was acquired by Parcelhero. From April 2024 Łukasz continued on the same platform and with the same team as Technical Lead, so his time on that platform is one continuous stretch of about 13 years, starting in 2013. Someone saying '13 years at Parcelhero' is describing this correctly.
Why he is leaving Parcelhero: his time there has come to an end and he is looking for his next role. There is no other reason to give.
peopleManagement: No people management at ParcelVision or Parcelhero; there he led technology choices and his own projects. At Fastlane International he was Software Development Manager and helped junior developers find their feet as the team grew.
recentEvidence: Over the last year he put AI into production using LLMs and embeddings, backed by observability, evals and experiments.
He brought AI into one of the core parts of the platform.
He led the platform's move to Kubernetes.
He helped migrate the platform from GCP to Azure.
titleReason: At ParcelVision and Parcelhero he stayed hands-on by choice: as the first engineering hire there he led technology decisions and his own projects instead of moving into people management. (At Fastlane International, earlier, he was Software Development Manager.)
